headline: Learned sequence models tested on unseen enzyme labels and variant pathogenicity
label: Learned Sequence Function Inference
summary: Label-scarce and unseen-label regimes now test whether learned sequence representations generalize beyond their training annotations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned sequence representations applied to functional annotation, with generalization beyond training labels as the explicit test. EnzPlacer uses contrastive learning to predict the first three EC number levels for enzymes whose fourth-level EC number is absent from training data. HATTER pairs modular active learning with human-in-the-loop annotation and reports supervised-level enzyme function prediction with less data. A benchmark of foundation and deep learning models, including SegmentNT, Enformer, Borzoi, SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, and STEP2h, evaluates splice site and exon annotation. Two published studies address variant pathogenicity: a deep neural network classifying driver versus passenger missense mutations across 30 PAN-cancer types, and PON-Del, a gradient boosting predictor for short sequence-retaining deletions. What is new is the emphasis on label-scarce and unseen-label regimes, though the summaries do not report benchmark detail, so comparative performance claims remain unassessed.
